notes_sections.title: Basic Concept of LCM and HCF
notes_sections.content: HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers exactly. LCM (Least Common Multiple) is the smallest number that is exactly divisible by the given numbers.

notes_sections.title: Finding HCF by Listing Factors
notes_sections.content: Write all factors of each number. The greatest common factor among them is the HCF. Example: Factors of 12 are 1,2,3,4,6,12. Factors of 18 are 1,2,3,6,9,18. So HCF = 6.

notes_sections.title: Finding LCM by Listing Multiples
notes_sections.content: Write first few multiples of each number. The smallest common multiple is the LCM. Example: Multiples of 4 are 4,8,12,16,20. Multiples of 6 are 6,12,18,24. So LCM = 12.

notes_sections.title: Prime Factor Method (Simple Form)
notes_sections.content: Break numbers into prime factors. For HCF take common primes. For LCM take all primes. Example: 8 = 2×2×2 and 12 = 2×2×3. HCF = 4, LCM = 24.

notes_sections.title: ₹ Based Simple Example
notes_sections.content: If ₹12 and ₹18 are to be divided equally into maximum groups, find HCF = 6. If two bells ring every 4 and 6 minutes, they ring together after LCM(4,6)=12 minutes.

notes_sections.title: Important Formula
notes_sections.content: For two numbers: LCM × HCF = Product of the numbers.

notes_sections.title: Common Mistakes
notes_sections.content: Confusing factors with multiples, assuming bigger number is always LCM, and forgetting to check common factors properly.

notes_sections.title: Quick Summary
notes_sections.content: HCF is used for equal distribution problems. LCM is used for repetition or cycle problems. Always check whether the question asks for grouping or meeting together.

tricks.title: If One Number Divides the Other
tricks.explanation: If bigger number is divisible by smaller number, then HCF is smaller and LCM is bigger.

tricks.title: Consecutive Numbers Rule
tricks.explanation: Two consecutive numbers always have HCF = 1.

tricks.title: Co-prime Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If two numbers have no common factor except 1, HCF=1 and LCM=product.

tricks.title: Use Product Formula
tricks.explanation: If HCF is known, quickly find LCM using product formula.

tricks.title: Small Multiples Method
tricks.explanation: For small numbers, just list first 4–5 multiples.

tricks.title: Even Number Check
tricks.explanation: If both numbers are even, 2 is definitely a common factor.
tricks.example: 8 and 14 → both even, so HCF at least 2.

tricks.title: Same Numbers Rule
tricks.explanation: If both numbers are same, HCF and LCM are that number itself.

tricks.title: ₹ Equal Distribution Trick
tricks.explanation: Whenever money is divided equally, think of HCF.

tricks.title: Meeting Together Trick
tricks.explanation: When events repeat and meet again, think of LCM.
tricks.example: Events after 5 and 7 days meet after LCM=35 days.

tricks.title: Prime Check Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If both numbers are prime and different, HCF=1.
